coverage.reviews: H-Net (1993–2026, 46,798 reviews) and Reviews in History (1996–2025, 2,459)
coverage.journals: Crossref metadata for 431 selected journal/title contexts (1,030,789 records); research candidates are journal-article records of at least ten pages using deposited or explicitly sourced publisher ranges, with an article-number exception for the Journal of Digital History

caveats: Counts measure participation, not influence; a review is not agreement.

Mapping networks, subject headings and journals to atlas entries is editorial and partly unreviewed; journal counts are venue-level (a journal tagged with a field counts all its qualifying research candidates).
These corpora are not the profession: H-Net is US-centred from 1993, Reviews in History is British, and Crossref coverage is uneven.

families.note: Families are editorial groupings. A field that bridges two families counts in both, so family shares overlap and must not be summed. The headline strip is the exception: it splits each item across its primary families.

sensitivity.note: An offline audit reproduces every published journal bin. Compared with the ten-page default, thresholds of eight, twelve or fifteen pages move each family’s 2000–2024 share by at most 0.4 percentage points. Using directory subjects without journal-level themes moves a share by as much as 5.3 points. Neither scenario verifies article genres.
sensitivity.pagination_note: Calculated lengths are missing for 25% of journal-article records in 1900-1949, 21% of journal-article records in 1950-1999, 9% of journal-article records in 2000-2024. Source coverage can change comparisons across time; genres remain unverified.
